subject: Copywriting
title: The Inverted Pyramid
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Inverted Pyramid usable.

hook.text: Journalists put the most important fact first. Email copywriters should too. The pyramid is widest at the top.

buildup.text: Average email reading time is 11 seconds. If the first sentence doesn't hook, the rest is never read.

discovery.text: The inverted pyramid: lead with the value, then provide context, then the CTA. Most emails fail by burying the point.

twist.text: Many marketers write emails like essays—building to a conclusion. But readers don't scroll. They scan.

climax.text: Amazon's internal emails are famously blunt: the point first, the evidence second. Bezos calls them 'narratives.'

punchline.text: Eleven seconds. Lead with the point or lose the reader.

quiz.question: What is the average time someone spends reading an email?

details.summary: The inverted pyramid places the most important information at the top of the email and narrows toward a call to action. Borrowed from journalism, this structure respects the reader's limited time, delivers value immediately, and guides attention toward the desired action with visual and logical...
details.whyItMatters: Most email recipients scan rather than read. The inverted pyramid ensures the key message reaches even the fastest scanners, maximizing both comprehension and conversion.
takeaways: Place the most important message at the very top of the email
Each section narrows focus toward the single call to action
The structure works for both HTML visual emails and plain text

faq.question: How does the inverted pyramid apply to email design?
faq.answer: Start with a bold header or key takeaway, follow with supporting detail, and end with a focused CTA button. The visual layout should literally narrow — wider content at top, concentrated action at bottom — guiding the eye toward the conversion point.

faq.question: Does the inverted pyramid work for storytelling emails?
faq.answer: Not as well. Story emails follow narrative arcs that build to a climax. The inverted pyramid works best for announcement, promotional, and informational emails where the reader needs to quickly assess relevance and take action.
